proof.text: Use the recorded normalized ordinary and derived scalar adjunctions and the normalized single-exponent identifications. The quotient unit and Kummer unit are fields of these identifications; they do not need to be reproved by a new resolution. On exact restriction functors, prove the compatibility of the composition comparison with the degree-zero single comparison directly through the localization factorization, degree by degree. Its shifted version follows from the existing exact-functor shift coherence.

The degree-zero complexes of Q_m and H_m are bounded above with flat terms (the other terms are zero). Apply the existing bounded-flat criterion at independent site and coefficient universes. Therefore the model counit ordinarySingle is invertible on each. The normalized derived adjunction unit, composed with ordinarySingle and the restriction/single comparison, is the image of the ordinary tensor unit. Evaluating the latter gives x ↦ 1 tensor x in the actual sheafified tensor product.

The transitivity comparison is the uniqueness isomorphism between the composite normalized left adjoint and the direct normalized left adjoint, as in the recorded successive-quotient normalization. The unit identity for uniqueness of left adjoints shows that the two successive adjuncts of its composite with any morphism equal the direct adjunct, after the actual restriction-composition comparison. Transport this identity through each single-exponent identification.

Conjugate transitivity by the normalized identifications to obtain isomorphisms c_F and c_B. Divide c_F by the invertible ordinarySingle on Q_m; full faithfulness of the degree-zero single functor recovers an ordinary isomorphism e_F. Divide c_B by the shift comparison followed by the shifted ordinarySingle on H_m; full faithfulness of the shifted single functor recovers e_H. These constructions give both required derived comparison equations. No separate local surjectivity or tensor-quotient identification is required to prove invertibility.

Let beta_Q be the ordinary adjunct of e_F, using the model object equality. The normalized unit computation in Step 2 identifies its image under the single functor with the derived adjunct of c_F. Combine Step 3, the exact-restriction single comparison, naturality, and the two quotient-unit fields. The result is p_m followed by restriction of beta_Q and the ordinary restriction comparison equals the endpoint equality followed by p_n. Faithfulness descends this equation to ordinary sheaves. On sections, the ordinary unit is 1 tensor x; tensor balancing and linearity extend the formula to b tensor x, proving the quotient formula.

Let beta be the ordinary adjunct of e_H. The scalar adjunction commutes with shifts by its induced left-adjoint shift structure. Shift Step 2 and combine it with Step 3 and the shifted exact-restriction comparison. The Kummer-unit fields then give delta_m followed by the shifted single image of the underlying integral map b_int equals the endpoint equality followed by delta_n. This is a boundary compatibility equation, not a cancellation of a Kummer boundary.

Put d=m/n. Since n*d=m and i_m followed by multiplication by m is zero, d times the composite of i_m with the endpoint equality factors uniquely through the kernel i_n. Call this factor b_0. The triple (b_0, d times the endpoint equality, the endpoint equality) is a morphism of the two Kummer short exact complexes. Naturality of the canonical short-exact-sequence triangle gives delta_m followed by the shifted single image of b_0 equals the endpoint equality followed by delta_n.

Multiplication by n annihilates the restricted H_n since i_n is mono; therefore multiplication by m annihilates it. Any map from B_m to that sheaf is zero, because multiplication by m on B_m is epi. Apply the exact Hom sequence of the rotated Kummer triangle: this vanishing makes precomposition with delta_m injective on maps between the relevant shifted single objects. Steps 6 and 7 therefore identify b_int and b_0 by full faithfulness of the single functor and the shift. Evaluating b_0 followed by i_n gives the required d=m/n formula with its fixed sign. The ordinary-adjunction unit and tensor balancing give the remaining formula for e_H on pure tensors.

title: Modulus change of the derived quotient and torsion identifications
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with a final object [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $m,n\geq1$ with $n\mid m$, put $R_q=(\mathbf Z/q\mathbf Z)_{\mathcal C}$ and let $\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}$ be the constant integer sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and derived scalar extension with its restriction adjunction [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Let
$$a_K:(K\otimes_{\mathbf Z}^{\mathbf L}R_m)\otimes_{R_m}^{\mathbf L}R_n\xrightarrow{\sim}K\otimes_{\mathbf Z}^{\mathbf L}R_n$$
be the canonical transitivity isomorphism of [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization] for the ring maps $\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}\to R_m\to R_n$. Let $F,B_0$ be abelian sheaves such that multiplication by each of $m,n$ is injective on $F$ and surjective on $B_0$. Put $H_q=\ker(q:B_0\to B_0)$ and $\bar F_q=F/qF$. Assume that $H_m$ and $\bar F_m$ are flat $R_m$-module sheaves, meaning their tensor functors on module sheaves preserve short exact sequences [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Under the quotient and normalized torsion identifications
$$F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}^{\mathbf L}R_q\simeq\bar F_q[0],\qquad B_0\otimes_{\mathbf Z}^{\mathbf L}R_q\simeq H_q[1]$$
of [lem-sfb-divisible-extension-derived-reduction] ($q=m,n$), $a_F$ and $a_{B_0}$ induce isomorphisms
$$\bar F_m\otimes_{R_m}R_n\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar F_n,\quad \bar f\otimes\bar b\longmapsto bf\bmod nF,$$
$$H_m\otimes_{R_m}R_n\xrightarrow{\sim}H_n,\quad h\otimes\bar b\longmapsto b(m/n)h.$$
In multiplicative notation the second formula on $h\otimes1$ is $h\mapsto h^{m/n}$. The normalization is the one for which the scalar-extension unit on $B_0$ is the connecting morphism of $0\to H_q\to B_0\xrightarrow{q}B_0\to0$.
